column6: Close on the woman at her typewriter at her desk in the ministry, her determined expression, fingers striking the keys, the cream memo in the platen; green CRT glow and a warm desk lamp on her face.

A long round duct corridor in the ministry lined with clocks all showing different times: the man, late, runs with his guitar case against a stream of faceless clerks in hats walking the other way; motion, coat flying, dozens of clock faces on the curved walls.

In the ministry hall: the torn scraps of his time card swirl up from his hands and turn into small white paper birds flying up toward the high ceiling; a streamer of paper tape among them reads BUT I DON'T CARE WHAT IT COSTS; faceless clerks look up. Keep BUT I DON'T CARE WHAT IT COSTS exactly.

Close at her desk: a small black sewing machine stitches a pair of red-and-cream striped trousers out of ribbons of rose and coral light that flow from her laughter; her laughing face soft in the background; the man in grey watching in amazement; warm glow over the grey desk.

Wide in the ministry hall: ribbons of rose, coral, mustard and teal colour flow out from the couple in the centre across the whole hall, curling over the filing walls and green CRT screens, warming the haze; a few of the faceless clerks' black hats have turned coral and mustard; the man and the woman in their colourful clothes laugh in the middle.

Close, low: their clasped hands as they run down the ministry aisle, his striped trousers and her coral dress and red shoes mid-stride, his guitar case swinging, ribbons of colour trailing behind them over the polished floor; rows of black hats blurred on either side.

On the road across the clouds: the cloud delegates from the convention (small white clouds with simple faces and little black bowler hats, one holding a name card reading CUMULUS) line the roadside and wave their hats as the man and the woman walk past hand in hand; open sky, warm sun, no machinery. Keep CUMULUS exactly.

Close two-shot high in the open sky: the man and the woman side by side, faces lit warm by the sun, wind lifting her coral ribbon and his teal scarf, both smiling at the road ahead; soft clouds behind, no machinery.
